title: Why Do Supercar Doors Open Upward?
description:
Your car door opens sideways, like a door in a house. A Lamborghini door goes straight up. A Mercedes from the nineteen fifties opens like the wings of a seagull. A McLaren door swings up and out like a butterfly. They look like showing off, but most of them started as an engineering problem. Today, ten parts of upward opening doors, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:07 1. The scissor doors
2:23 2. The gullwing doors
3:34 3. The butterfly doors
4:39 4. The rotating doors
5:47 5. The falcon wing doors
6:55 6. The high sill
8:00 7. The gas struts
9:06 8. The roof cut
10:12 9. The torsion bars
11:19 10. The rollover bolts
12:17 The verdict

- Mercedes-Benz 300 SL space frame and gullwing doors: Wikipedia, "Mercedes-Benz 300 SL" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_300_SL
- Butterfly doors and McLaren F1 central seat: Wikipedia, "Butterfly doors" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butterfly_doors and "McLaren F1" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_F1
- Koenigsegg dihedral synchro-helix doors: Wikipedia, "Koenigsegg" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koenigsegg

- DeLorean torsion bars (Grumman, cryogenic treatment): Wikipedia, "DeLorean DMC-12" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeLorean_DMC-12
- SLS AMG rollover pyrotechnic hinges: Wikipedia, "Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_SLS_AMG
